chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He was asked about a man who was prevented from having intercourse with his wife, so he could not approach her. He said: 'If he is unable to approach other women, he should not keep her except with her consent to that. And if he is able to approach other women, there is no harm in keeping her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a husband who cannot consummate his marriage with his specific wife?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding *al-tadlis* (concealment of defects) in marriage, the scholar distinguishes between a man's general capacity for intimacy and his specific limitation. If the man is impotent with all women, he retains the wife only with her consent to the condition; however, if he is capable with others, he may keep her without such restriction, emphasizing that the defect is relative to his specific spouse rather than an absolute impediment.
